title: Page 32 signed-displacement block-reversal holdout

target.description: Whether the final two negative generated displacements prescribe reversing blocks 15 and 16

summary: The predicted RR orientation ranked third of four on the withheld pair and failed both frozen acceptance conditions.
why_run: To test the negative-sign-as-reversal interpretation without language scoring or post-hoc transformations.

pipeline.description: Train a first-order GP29 transition model on blocks 1-14 and score DD, DR, RD, and RR on blocks 15-16, with adjacent-pair leave-out controls.

acceptance.criterion: RR is best and its margin exceeds every corresponding adjacent-pair control.

controls: No block swap, reverse-register substitution, cyclic shift, or phonetic branching was allowed.
Fourteen adjacent block pairs supplied leave-pair-out comparison controls.
interpretation: Within the exact tested model and pairing, negative displacement is not supported as an instruction to reverse the final two rune blocks.
limitations: The original implementation was not preserved, so the published score ledger and decision are auditable but the model cannot yet be independently regenerated from source.
The conclusion does not reject other predeclared meanings of sign outside this slice.
The full rune transcription and forward next-slice instructions are excluded from the public package.

normalization_changes: Converted historical fields to the HMS run schema.
Preserved the contract, report, result, and score ledger as normalized UTF-8 text.
Excluded the full rune transcription and forward next-slice instructions.

raw_artifacts.reason: The source transcription is identified by hash but not redistributed; forward research instructions are withheld.
